packageRules.description: Digest and patch updates land in a single weekly PR (Monday before 9am, Europe/Paris) instead of one PR, hence one Tests run, each; minor and major updates keep their own PR, at any time. Our own images are left out: their rules below take every build as soon as it is published and automerge it. The stateless images and the GitHub Actions of the next two rules leave this PR for their own weekly one, which automerges. The rules below that set a groupName (beszel, pangolin-role-dependencies, socket-proxy, immich-role-dependencies) come later and win, so those groups keep their own PR, on this weekly schedule for their digest and patch updates. A path_bypass_images.json version shares its compose image's depName and update type, so both stay in this PR, which carries the re-read note of the last rule and is merged by hand. rebaseWhen is conflicted for every branch (top level): the main ruleset does not require an up-to-date branch (strict_required_status_checks_policy = false, tofu/github/ruleset_homelab.tf), so rebasing every open PR on each push to main would only rerun its checks and cancel the running ones; a PR is rebased only when it conflicts

Stateless images (no database of their own, no schema migration on start): their digest and patch updates leave the weekly PR for a second weekly PR, merged by Renovate (GitHub auto-merge, platformAutomerge) once the checks the main ruleset requires pass (Ansible lint, OpenTofu lint, CI lint, Tests); the merge deploys them (deploy-docker-app.yaml). Molecule never pulls an image, so the checks do not prove it starts: a missing image fails the deploy run, one that starts then crashes leaves it green (dc@ is active once docker compose up runs) and only its Uptime Kuma monitor goes DOWN; roll back with a revert that also drops the image from this list, or Renovate re-merges the same digest the next Monday. A listed image restarts its whole compose project (dc@ restart), databases included: hence matchFileNames leaves out flip_planning, whose nginx assets sidecar and mailpit would restart the three Flip Planning instances, production and its Postgres included, nearly every week (they stay in the manual weekly PR); nginx_demo's restart takes its demo Postgres along, accepted. An allowlist, not a denylist: an image not listed here, or a minor or major update, stays manual. Never listed: databases, redis/valkey, meilisearch, an app whose image migrates its own data (Immich, Nextcloud, Monica, Paperless-ngx, Dawarich, Karakeep, planning-equipes, Jellyfin, Beszel, Pangolin...), an image of path_bypass_images.json (its public paths are re-read by a human before the merge, see the last rule), Traefik, the socket proxy and vmauth (edge and security sidecars), an image whose updates a later groupName rule takes (immich-role-dependencies, pangolin-role-dependencies, beszel, vector, blocky, borgmatic: that group would never automerge anyway), an app with a database of its own even when it is reset (betisier), and a frontend released in lockstep with a reviewed backend (meerkat-crm-frontend, whose backend is in path_bypass_images.json: automerging it alone would skew the two). nginx: the static nginx_demo. gotenberg and tika: Paperless-ngx's converters, inert while Paperless is paused (a later rule disables its role). karakeep-chrome: Karakeep's headless Chromium, a crawler without volume (Karakeep itself, its Meilisearch and the karakeep image of path_bypass_images.json stay manual). rclone: kdrive_sync's one-shot `docker compose run --rm`, no state but its obscured config rewritten on every run, on the NAS whose playbook is run by hand (the merge deploys nothing there). debian: the base of the Molecule image (ansible/molecule/_shared/Dockerfile), never deployed, and the PR's Tests build it and run every scenario on it

GitHub Actions (uses: of the workflows and composite actions, pinned by digest with their version in a comment): patch updates join the stateless automerged PR. Not digest updates: under an unchanged version tag, a new digest means the tag was moved, the very attack the SHA pin guards against (tj-actions/changed-files, March 2025), and an automerged action runs in deploy-docker-app's production job, next to SOPS_AGE_KEY and the deploy SSH key; those stay in the manual weekly PR. The PR's own Lint and Tests run them, except the steps only deploy-docker-app, restore-test, borg-check and storage-box-quota run: those break on their next run after the merge, which fails visibly. Container images and runner labels of the workflows are not actions (depType docker, container, service, github-runner) and stay manual

Stateful images: a MAJOR upgrade changes the on-disk format of the data they keep. PostgreSQL (and postgis, Immich's postgres) refuses to start on a data directory of the previous major (scanopy 17 -> 18 would have left it down: dump/restore or pg_upgrade first); MariaDB/MySQL need mariadb-upgrade and have no way back (the official mariadb image is also held on its LTS line by the next rule); Meilisearch refuses ANY other version's database, patch included, so Karakeep sets MEILI_UPGRADE_DB for minor and patch bumps, and a major may need a dump/import; Redis/Valkey change their RDB/AOF format. Renovate only lists these on the Dependency Dashboard and opens the PR once its box is ticked, so a migration is planned instead of merged as a routine bump. Minor, patch and digest updates are unaffected. Regexes because the same image is written docker.io/postgres, docker.io/library/postgres or postgres depending on the compose file

Nextcloud's database (official mariadb image) stays on the 12.3 LTS line (maintained until June 2029). 13.0 and the releases after it are rolling releases, superseded every quarter with no bug-fix release of their own, and a MariaDB major has no way back. Raise the bound to the next LTS once MariaDB announces it, and plan that upgrade (mariadb-upgrade, run by MARIADB_AUTO_UPGRADE) as a migration. linuxserver/mariadb (11.8 LTS) is another package, not affected

Redis builds -bookworm tags only up to the 8.2 line (8.4 and later are trixie or alpine; 8.4.0-bookworm is a stale February 2026 tag, never patched since). Without this cap Renovate offers 8.4.0-bookworm to Nextcloud's cache, older than the 8.2.x it runs, and that minor update shares the renovate/redis-8.x branch with Dawarich's 7.4 -> 8 major, so the major's dashboard approval holds it too. Moving off bookworm is a deliberate tag change, not a bump. A regex, not "<8.3": a suffixed tag is valid npm semver (a prerelease), which no plain range satisfies, so "<8.3" would also drop the 8.2 patches
Beszel: the hub, the agent image (plain and -alpine) and the agent binary of the newt LXC (beszel_agent defaults) move together, an agent newer or older than its hub is not supported

Vector (log_agent): the image of the container agents and the binary of the newt LXC (log_agent defaults, whose sha256 must be updated by hand) move together, so every host runs the configuration the Molecule scenario log_agent_lxc tested with that binary

Blocky: the image of the Pi and the binary of the newt LXC (blocky role defaults) move together, the two DNS resolvers of the house stay on one version. A bump also needs blocky_binary_sha256 (blocky_checksums.txt of the release), or get_url refuses the archive and Molecule fails. Merging deploys the Pi (pi.yml), lxc.yml is run by hand
Group all Pangolin role dependencies together

newt only reaches Docker through the allowlist of newt-socket-proxy (ansible/roles/newt/defaults/main.yml, #853), read off newt 1.19.0's docker/docker.go: a bump that calls another endpoint empties Pangolin's container list
prBodyNotes: Avant de merger : relire `docker/docker.go` de cette version de newt contre `newt_socket_proxy_allow_get` / `_allow_head` (`ansible/roles/newt/defaults/main.yml`). Après déploiement, `docker logs newt-socket-proxy` ne doit refuser que des `containers/<id>/json`.

packageRules.description: The socket proxy sidecar of beszel_agent and of newt is one image: without this rule (after pangolin-role-dependencies, so it wins) newt's copy would ride in that group and beszel_agent's in the weekly one, two PRs whose digests drift apart
Pangolin's Docker tags are prefixed with ee- (e.g. ee-1.21.0); teach Renovate to parse them as semver so EE updates are detected

Badger v1.8.0 fails Traefik's plugin integrity check (traefik/traefik#14115): Traefik disables the plugin, the badger@file middleware vanishes and every Pangolin router returns 404. Upstream says to stay on v1.7.0; drop this rule once Traefik fixes it
The Hetzner Storage Box only runs a borg 1.x server (ansible/roles/borgmatic/tasks/host.yml): a borg 2 client cannot talk to it

borgmatic runs from pipx on the Debian hosts and from its official image on the NAS (ansible/roles/borgmatic/templates/compose.yaml), whose tag is the borgmatic version: both, and the Molecule image's borgmatic, move together
Group all Immich role dependencies together

planning-equipes is our own image: no 1 day cooldown, take updates as soon as they are published. Merging on main triggers the deploy workflow. The custom manager sets depType to the channel (release or main, see the flip_planning role defaults)
Production (flip_planning) follows the published releases. semver versioning keeps only a full X.Y.Z: main, latest, sha-xxxxxxx and the floating X.Y tag are ignored
Patch and minor releases automerge once the lint workflow passes, and so deploy to production

A major release is never deployed on its own (YAML scenario format, environment variables, irreversible Flyway migrations): the PR waits for a manual merge. So does a digest change behind an existing X.Y.Z tag, which should not happen with immutable releases
The demo (demo_planning) runs the latest main: every new digest automerges once the lint workflow passes

promptoramix is our own image (the Linkx tournament AI, deployed on flip by ansible/roles/promptoramix), published by its CI on every push to main and followed through the main tag: no 1 day cooldown, take updates as soon as they are published, except during the tournament wave (Thursday 00:00-12:00 Europe/Paris), when a restart would forfeit the games in progress

The first digest pin and every new main digest automerge once the lint workflow passes; merging on main triggers the deploy workflow (dc@ only pulls a missing image, so the digest is what rolls out a new build)
path_bypass_images.json notes the version each app's public paths were read off (tofu/pangolin_config/tests/invariants.tftest.hcl). Its custom manager has no digest to pin: the compose file pins it

TREK: the image stays docker.io/mauriceboe/trek, but the GitHub repository moved from mauriceboe/TREK to liketrek/TREK (the old name only redirects): release notes and changelogs come from the new one

Karakeep Button, the FreshRSS extension of the rss role: third-party code (veverkap, neither FreshRSS nor Karakeep) run inside FreshRSS, with no release since its Karakeep port, followed by commit on main. git-refs gives no release timestamp, so the 1 day cooldown would hold every update forever. Never automerged: read the diff, then update rss_karakeep_button_sha256 by hand (get_url refuses any other archive, Molecule fails until then)

Python reste en 3.14 tant que PyYAML n'a pas de wheel cp315 (yaml/pyyaml#981, #994 ; la CI fait uv sync --no-build) et qu'ansible-core ne liste pas 3.15 comme Python de contrôleur (#722). Retirer la règle alors, et rafraîchir uv.lock (cffi >= 2.1.1, markupsafe >= 3.0.4, rpds-py >= 2026.9.1, pyyaml), que la PR Python de Renovate ne touche pas. matchPackageNames compare le packageName (python/cpython pour mise, actions/python-versions pour setup-python), pas le depName python commun aux deux

Paused apps (docs/runbooks/app-en-pause.md): no PR for an app that does not run. Paperless-ngx (paperless_enabled: false in host_vars/docker): every image of its role, gotenberg and tika included (they run nowhere else). Resuming the app removes this rule and the next one in the same PR, and Renovate then proposes the versions published meanwhile. The Keycloak bench of flip_planning (demo_planning_kc, paused too) needs no rule: its two images are written in ansible/flip.yml on the mobile pr-72 tag, which no manager reads, and the compose template it shares with production and the demo must stay tracked

Paused apps, second half: the Paperless-ngx entry of path_bypass_images.json. The rule above only covers the role's files, and the custom manager would otherwise bump the json alone, a PR the path_bypasses_follow_their_image tofu test always fails (compose and json no longer at the same version). Removed together with the rule above

Guard, kept last: an update of path_bypass_images.json never automerges, and its PR says what to re-read before the manual merge (this note replaced the path-bypass-review.yaml workflow and its relecture-chemins-publics environment on 2026-10-29). Renovate automerges a branch only if every update in it does, so an image added there later blocks its whole group (compose and json share the depName, hence the group) instead of skipping the re-read
prBodyNotes: **Chemins publics sans SSO** : cette PR monte une image de `tofu/pangolin_config/path_bypass_images.json`. Avant de merger, pour chaque entrée dont `version` change, lire les notes de version (`releases`) et, dans les sources de la nouvelle version, les fichiers listés dans `reread`. Une route non authentifiée apparue sous un préfixe de `paths`, ou un partage déplacé : corriger les `_paths` de l'appli (`tofu/pangolin_config/website_<app>.tf`) dans cette PR.

customManagers.description: Track the planning-equipes images pinned in the Ansible role defaults (plain vars, no manager covers them); the variable suffix becomes the depType: release (flip_planning) or main (demo_planning)
Track Traefik experimental plugin versions in the Pangolin static config (e.g. fosrl/badger); no built-in manager covers Traefik plugins

The version each image's public paths were read off (tofu/pangolin_config/path_bypass_images.json). Same depName as in the compose file, so both land in the same PR: the tofu test stays green, and the PR (never automerged, see the last packageRules entry) is merged by hand once the release notes and the sources listed in reread have been read. No commit by hand

Versions pinned in Ansible role defaults with a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment on the line above (borg, borgmatic, newt, the Beszel agent binary, the Vector binary of log_agent, the Blocky binary): no built-in manager reads plain vars. A borg, newt, Beszel agent, Vector or Blocky bump also needs its sha256 updated by hand (the release lists them), or get_url refuses the download
OLM image started by `docker run` in the composite action olm-tunnel (used by deploy-docker-app and ping), pinned by tag and digest; the github-actions manager only reads `uses:`
Images pinned by tag and digest in plain vars of the pangolin role defaults: geoipupdate (weekly GeoLite2 update) and crowdsec (agent + LAPI + AppSec of the pangolin stack)

Beszel agent images of the beszel_agent role (plain and -alpine, the one with smartctl), pinned by tag and digest in plain vars of its defaults: the compose template keeps a single `image:` key, two of them in one service would leave one untracked once Renovate strips the Jinja
Blocky image of the blocky role (the Pi's container), pinned by tag and digest in a plain var of its defaults, next to the binary of the newt LXC
Commit of the Karakeep Button FreshRSS extension pinned in the rss role defaults (no release to follow): Renovate proposes the new head of main
